title: Sign Here: Attributing a Source for a More Trustworthy Software Supply Chain
abstract: arXiv:2610.28794v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Software supply chain attacks continue to be on the rise, exploiting the trust that helps open source ecosystems thrive. Recent incidents like the Shai-Hulud worm and the Axios compromise demonstrate that a single malicious package can have wide reaching and devastating impacts overnight. These high profile attacks can be traced back to the same culprit: package registries. Although they are a useful convenience to pull prebuilt packages from, is such a commonly exploited component of the software supply chain worth the risk? In this paper, we investigate whether removing the registry from the developer workflow by building packages directly from source can serve as a malware prevention strategy - effectively removing an entire attack surface. Our hypothesis is that malicious packages avoid attributing a source to minimize visibility, while benign packages seek exposure and therefore link to their repositories. We evaluate this through

translated_abstract: 软件供应链攻击持续上升，利用了帮助开源生态系统蓬勃发展的信任机制。近期诸如 Shai-Hulud 蠕虫和 Axios 入侵等事件表明，单个恶意软件包可能在一夜之间造成广泛而毁灭性的影响。这些备受瞩目的攻击都可以追溯到同一个罪魁祸首：软件包注册中心（package registries）。尽管从注册中心拉取预构建软件包是一种便利，但作为软件供应链中经常被利用的组件，它值得冒这个风险吗？在本文中，我们研究了通过直接从源代码构建软件包、将注册中心从开发者工作流程中移除，是否可以作为恶意软件防御策略——从而有效消除整个攻击面。我们的假设是：恶意软件包避免标注源代码来源以最小化其可见性，而良性软件包则寻求曝光度，因此会链接到其代码仓库。我们通过以下方式进行评估：
tldr: 本文提出通过直接从源代码构建软件包来取代软件包注册中心，并利用“恶意软件包通常不标注源代码来源、而良性软件包会链接其代码仓库”这一假设，作为防范软件供应链恶意软件攻击的策略，从而消除整个攻击面。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes removing package registries from the developer workflow by building packages directly from source as a malware prevention strategy, based on the hypothesis that malicious packages avoid attributing a source while benign packages link to their repositories for exposure.
